Maria: Quick follow-up to the RFC — we need to pick between brokered service claims (short-lived tokens minted by a central broker) vs resource-scoped API keys (long-lived keys tied to a project/resource). Can we land on one? :thinking:
Kevin: Short summary from infra: brokered claims give better least-privilege and rotation, but add operational complexity and a network hop. Resource-scoped keys are simpler for customers and offline jobs.
Jordan: Perf note: broker adds an extra hop on job start unless we cache claims. That interacts with autoscaler cold-starts and throughput.
Sam: From product: customers like the simplicity of a single long-lived key for scripts. They care less about rotation if revocation is possible.
Priya (SRE): Ops concern: long-lived keys increase blast radius and slow revocation. Broker lets us revoke centrally. Need clear revocation / audit story either way.
Maria: Proposed hybrid: issue long-lived opaque "handle" keys to clients, but require a broker exchange to mint short-lived resource-scoped claims for use. Client holds handle, broker mints short TTL claim on-demand. Example exchange flow:
```
# Client sends handle to broker
POST /v1/auth/exchange
Authorization: RedwoodHandle h=hh_abc123
Body: { "resource": "org/42/project/7/runner" }
# Broker responds with short-lived claim
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Authorization: RedwoodClaim c=cc_456 ttl=60
{ "jwt": "eyJhbGci...", "ttl": 60 }
```
Kevin: Sounds good. Note: handles are sensitive — if leaked attacker could perform exchanges. Suggest HMAC-binding so broker only accepts handles with proof or origin tag.
Jordan: Implementation sketch: broker validates handle sig, checks quotas, returns signed JWT claim with org/project scope + nonce. TTL in 30s–120s. Add local cache keyed by (handle, resource) to reduce exchange frequency for repeated short-lived ops. Also include exchange-rate limiting.
Maria: Migration plan: phase 1 — support handle exchange for cross-project and platform jobs only; phase 2 — opt-in for single-project flows; phase 3 — full deprecate of legacy long-lived admin keys. Canary on Dedicated customers first.
Priya (SRE): Runbook: if broker outage, fallback to read-only resource-scoped keys (no write operations) and emit critical alert. Feature-flag broker per-tenant to disable during rollouts. Also require a revocation propagation window SLA.
Sam: Metrics to track: exchange count, exchange latency (P50/P95), cache hit ratio, number of revoked handles, rate of failed exchanges, per-tenant exchange QPS. Add a security alert for abnormal exchange spikes.
auth-bot: Note created: RFC delta + security signoff + perf test matrix required. @Maria please attach checklist.
Maria: I'll draft the RFC delta and ops checklist. Who can pair on the perf matrix?
Kevin: I can own perf matrix with Jordan. Quick design Q: how do we store handles — deterministic (derive from org+key) vs random opaque? I prefer random opaque with pointer to metadata; reduces guessability.
Jordan: Agreed. Avoid DB hot keys by sharding handle lookup and using a TTL rotating cache. Track per-handle exchange counters for rate limiting.
Sam: UX: add CLI helpers `redwood auth exchange --handle H --resource R` and SDK helper to auto-exchange on use. Makes migration easier for customers.
Maria: Great. I'll add CLI/SDK proposal to the RFC delta. Goal: decision by EOW so we can schedule implementation next sprint. :rocket:
